calls.head: Who blinks first?
calls.body: The Red Wings are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Avalanche are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Red Wings’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
calls.call: The Red Wings’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.8 expected goals per 60 against the Avalanche.

calls.head: Who drives the play: the Avalanche
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Avalanche have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Red Wings around the middle. The ice should tilt the Avalanche’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

calls.head: The Avalanche’s defense joins the attack, the Red Wings’ stays home
calls.body: On shots from defensemen, Colorado is one of the league’s best, but Detroit is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Avalanche’s defensemen jump into the play.

COL.head: We gave Colorado a 61% chance, and they delivered.

DET.head: We gave Detroit only a 39% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Colorado shut down Detroit’s power play
surprises.body: Detroit’s power play created 2.0 expected goals per 60, against their usual 8.8 (about 8.1 against Colorado) and a league average of 7.8. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

surprises.head: A shutout for Mackenzie Blackwood
surprises.body: Blackwood stopped all 27 shots, worth 2.1 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 15 starts.

story.head: Blackwood blanks the Red Wings
paras: Martin Nečas and Nathan MacKinnon scored power-play goals less than three minutes apart midway through the second to put the Avalanche up 2-0. Nečas scored his second of the night early in the third to make it 3-0. Gabriel Landeskog and Moritz Seider dropped the gloves midway through the period. For Seider, it was his first fight since November 2025. Cale Makar stretched the lead to 4-0 on the power play later in the period. MacKinnon finished with a goal and two assists, and Nečas added two assists for a four-point night.
The Avalanche carried the play, and got the result to match. Mackenzie Blackwood was perfect for the Avs, 27 saves on 27 shots, and Daniil Tarasov stopped 25 of 29 at the other end.
The Avalanche went 3-for-5 on the power play. The Avalanche improved to 10-6-2 and climbed to third in the Central, while the Red Wings dropped to 7-8-3, still last in the Atlantic.
